answer: Capacity-Constrained Routing Graph Identities route transaction packets across a physical topology resembling a high-altitude mesa. Each node must forward traffic for neighbors to maintain local bandwidth, like a grazing path across an isolated mountain meadow. Sybil duplicates cannot share the same physical pipe without dropping packets. If an agent spawns copies, network congestion forces traffic over a restrictive computational ledge, exposing the duplicates via throughput degradation. Attackers pay hardware bandwidth costs and latency penalties for every cloned instance.
